chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
"Take the pebbles of the Jamarat from Jumm (Muzdalifah); if you take them from your saddlebag in Mina, it will suffice you."

key_terms.أَجْزَأَكَ: it will suffice you / be valid for you

ai.seo_question: Is it valid to take Hajj pebbles from Mina instead of Muzdalifah?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility in the ritual stoning (Rami) of the Jamarat, affirming that while collecting pebbles from Muzdalifah is the normative practice, taking them from one's saddlebag in Mina remains legally sufficient (ja'aza). This ruling underscores the practical ease (taysir) granted to pilgrims, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the validity of actions performed with sincere intention even if the specific method of collection varies. It highlights the juristic consensus on the permissibility of using pre-collected pebbles, thereby accommodating the logistical realities of the Hajj pilgrimage.
